title: I built a medieval archery FPS in Godot with Codex. We played 3v3 for hours while it added features mid-session
author: Fillup01
selftext:
This is a medieval archery FPS I've been building in Godot. I wanted the movement like CS Source style (bhopping, air strafing) and I wanted the bow to feel good, not crazy but just a bow that you can draw 0-100% and release that obeys gravity.

Most of the code was written by Codex via Astra, dabbled with claude code opus 5.5. I ended up convincing some friends to try to see if I could get multiplayer working and got a 3v3 by ziping a .exe and sending it to them on dropbox. They download unzip/launch and then menu just said connect to get into my pc as host.

We'd play a match then spit balling what is good and what is bad. Did like 5 iterations same process as a release lol.

  
Biggest pain was my friend decided to use claude code to put walls/spin bot into the .exe. hacking my game in real time.

Honestly this feels so fun. I've always wanted to get into game dev but it felt impossible coming from internal b2b app building corporate world. 

AI really is the great intellectual equalizer huh. We're about to go through the renaissance of everything as everyone that has an idea can build it. The mere volume of ideas that will be built will create a lot shit but also a lot of gold! Life's short, be a Gloomer

Curious of anyone else's vibe of the current state of ai game dev. Yay or Nay?
